title: Rucaparib (Rubraca) maintenance tablets
context_label: First-line maintenance after a platinum response
schedule_label: Take the prescribed dose twice daily, about 12 hours apart, every day. There is no planned week off.
schedule_summary: Take the prescribed dose twice daily, about 12 hours apart, every day. There is no planned week off. Start within eight weeks of the final platinum dose. Treatment lasts up to two years and may stop earlier if the cancer grows or side effects make continued treatment unsuitable.
purpose: Chemotherapy has reduced the cancer. These tablets aim to keep it under control for longer. Your team will explain how your response and tumour test results inform your options.
indication_text: First-line maintenance for adults whose stage III or IV high-grade epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer has responded completely or partially to platinum chemotherapy.
administration_text: Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with a large glass of water, with or without food. Leave a missed or vomited dose out and take only your next scheduled dose. Never crush the tablets or take extra to catch up.
monitoring_summary: A full blood count checks for anaemia, infection risk and bruising. Kidney and liver blood tests help detect side effects you may not feel.
review_status: Feasibility build. Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Rucaparib
agents.explanation: Blocks enzymes called PARP that help repair DNA. Some ovarian cancer cells depend on these repairs to survive.
agents.mechanism: Blocks enzymes called PARP that help repair DNA. Some ovarian cancer cells depend on these repairs to survive.
agents.watch: Call about persistent fatigue, breathlessness, infections or unusual bruising. Regular blood tests can detect problems before you feel unwell.
risks: Nausea, changes in taste or bowel habit
symptoms: Nausea, changes in taste or bowel habit

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Tiredness, changes in appetite and nausea can affect meals and daily activity. Tell your team early if you are eating or drinking less.

common_effects.title: At home
common_effects.text: Tell the team if constipation, diarrhoea or changes in taste persist.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts · Rucaparib
serious_effects.text: Phone urgently for fever or bleeding. Report unusual tiredness, breathlessness or bruising.

serious_effects.title: Nausea or bowel changes · Rucaparib
serious_effects.text: Tell the team if nausea, constipation or diarrhoea affects eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: Liver changes · Rucaparib
serious_effects.text: Blood tests can detect changes before symptoms. Report yellow skin or eyes promptly.

serious_effects.title: Sun sensitivity · Rucaparib
serious_effects.text: Cover exposed skin, use a high-factor sunscreen and report an intense skin reaction.

serious_effects.title: Changes in taste · Rucaparib
serious_effects.text: Mention persistent taste changes or loss of appetite so the team can help you eat enough.

serious_effects.title: Rare marrow disorders
serious_effects.text: Low counts that persist despite a treatment pause may need specialist tests. Rarely, a marrow disorder or leukaemia develops.

questions.q: What if I am sick after a tablet or miss a dose?
questions.a: Leave that dose out. Take the next scheduled dose only. Contact your team if vomiting continues or you cannot keep fluids down.

questions.q: What happens after this part of treatment?
questions.a: Start within eight weeks of the final platinum dose. Treatment lasts up to two years and may stop earlier if the cancer grows or side effects make continued treatment unsuitable.
Call the oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding, worsening breathlessness or vomiting that prevents drinking. Report unusual bruising or persistent fatigue promptly.

The platinum treatment has already reduced the cancer. Maintenance is a different treatment that aims to prolong that response. Your team can discuss the expected benefit, side effects and alternatives in your situation.

support.title: Rucaparib
support.text: Call about persistent fatigue, breathlessness, infections or unusual bruising. Regular blood tests can detect problems before you feel unwell.

support.title: At home
support.text: Use the morning and evening tablet plan. Ask about any new medicine, including over-the-counter medicines, before starting it. Protect exposed skin from sunlight.

support.title: Your anti-sickness plan
support.text: Rucaparib can cause nausea. Your team may prescribe a daily anti-sickness tablet and separate rescue treatment. Ask which one to take and when.

support.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Use effective contraception during treatment and for six months after the last dose if you could become pregnant. Avoid breastfeeding during treatment and for two weeks afterwards.

teachback: Can you show which tablets you would take tomorrow morning and what you would do after a missed dose?
consent_support: Discuss expected delay in progression, alternatives including observation where appropriate, effects on blood counts, and the rare risk of myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukaemia.
safety_note: Call the oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding, worsening breathlessness or vomiting that prevents drinking. Report unusual bruising or persistent fatigue promptly.
urgent_extra: Call the oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding, worsening breathlessness or vomiting that prevents drinking. Report unusual bruising or persistent fatigue promptly.

evidence.title: ATHENA-MONO · first-line rucaparib maintenance
evidence.interpretation: In the ATHENA-MONO trial, the time before the cancer grew or a participant died was about 20 months with rucaparib and 9 months with placebo at the middle of each group. Some people had shorter or longer periods.
evidence.limitations: The study has not established whether people live longer overall. Ask how your tumour results and the side effects you wish to avoid affect your choice.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: The team checks your blood count, kidney and liver function and pregnancy status where relevant.
Confirm your last platinum date and ask your pharmacist to check prescribed medicines, painkillers, supplements and herbal products.

rows.label: Each month
cells: A full blood count checks for anaemia, infection risk and bruising. Kidney and liver blood tests help detect side effects you may not feel.
Keep the appointment even when you feel well. If a result changes, extra blood tests or a pause may be needed.

rows.label: If treatment is paused
cells: Persistent low blood counts need closer monitoring and can require haematology review. Your team sets the timing of tests before restarting.
Record the stop date. Wait for your team to give you a new dose and restart date.

monitoring_schedule.note: Your team records the dates and arranges extra tests if your symptoms or results change.
